novelty_flags.label: Theorem: generic converse
novelty_flags.one_line: The consumer says that “unequal adoption propensity ... destroys future cohort forecasts” but identifies no published estimator or workflow that makes the refuted no-HDK extrapolation.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition: exact fiber gap
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed lower-bound witness targets “any method that ignores the hazard-algebra failure,” rather than a named published estimator or workflow.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition: collision gray zone
novelty_flags.one_line: The impossibility statement rules out generic confidence bands without naming a published root-N procedure whose asserted coverage or diameter it refutes.

soundness_flags.label: def:canonical-realization; thm:finite-realization; thm:hazard-lift-identification; def:fixed-chart-estimator
soundness_flags.one_line: Predictive rank of the full stopped Hankel array does not ensure that the predeclared chart H is nonsingular, yet the canonical map uses H^{-1}; moreover the empirical estimator invokes several inverses without a defined regular-neighborhood domain or measurable fallback when a sample chart/Gram/inverse is singular.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question: legal-lift frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: As written, singletonness is just equality of pi^0 over all legal lifts, and generic quantifier elimination after clearing denominators already gives a terminating semialgebraic decision procedure; the question needs a non-generic observable frontier or materially sharper complexity claim.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem: hazard-lift identification
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The result is conditional on known finite K, finite emissions, homogeneous untreated HMM dynamics, sequential hazard timing, rank/invertibility, and hazard constancy within exact emission-alias classes.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Conditional identification of finite cohort untreated path laws under the declared hazard-lift model; it does not identify latent labels or unrestricted staggered-adoption ATT.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem: fixed-chart inference
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Root-N inference is only claimed on a fixed, separated chart/frame stratum and expressly excludes the local collision gray zone.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Conditional fixed-grid asymptotic linearity and simultaneous coverage on the declared regular stratum, not uniform inference over rank/algebra collisions.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Proposition: exact fiber gap and collision gray zone
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The exact witness and local lower experiment are confined to K=3, T=5, g=0, r=1.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: A coordinate-specific positive nonidentification and weak-gap certificate, not a claim for every horizon or cohort.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question: Kim--Lee certificate
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The underlying application data are unavailable to this run, so no empirical pass/fail conclusion is asserted.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: A preregistered empirical decision question contingent on access to the Netflix--IPTV data.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies parametric-output HMMs with exactly two aliased states; Lemma 2 characterizes equivalent minimal realizations through a similarity family and Theorem 2 characterizes its feasible region. It contains no causal counterfactual or ATT target.

The article models informative dropout with a discrete event-history model and time-varying latent Markov heterogeneity, estimated through extended forward--backward recursions; it is not a causal observed-law invariance result.

The Netflix--IPTV application is a balanced monthly panel from March through November 2021; it has six treatment-evaluation dates after three covariate-only months and includes a binary any-VoD-viewing outcome alongside viewing-hour outcomes.

The preprint gives sufficient conditions for ATT identification without parallel trends using repeated outcomes and a more flexible unobserved-heterogeneity framework; it is an adjacent but different identification route.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2.2 and Section 2.4; Theorems 1--2 proof index
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies staggered-adoption group-time effects under an interactive fixed-effects model and unobserved-heterogeneity conditions, then supplies consistency and asymptotic-normality results; it does not use a stopped HMM alias fiber.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 225(2), 2021; publisher full text inaccessible in this review
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The record verifies the published venue/year and describes staggered-DiD identification, asymptotic properties, and a simultaneous bootstrap. No formula-level comparison was used for a flag because the version-of-record text was inaccessible.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make chart selection mathematically total: either add the selected-minor nonvanishing condition to the identification class, or specify a deterministic rank-revealing rule; define a measurable regular-neighborhood extension or fallback for every empirical inverse.

Recast the legal-lift OEQ around a non-generic output, such as a closed-form or low-dimensional invariant for a specified alias block, with complexity substantially sharper than general CAD/quantifier elimination.
Tie each negative result to a named published extrapolation or HMM-based causal workflow and state precisely which coverage, identification, or forecast claim fails under the positive fiber.
Add a worked positive K=3 example satisfying HDK and the fixed-chart conditions, so the causal identification theorem has an operational counterpart to its nonidentification witnesses.

recommended_next_step: Revise the canonical-chart/estimator domain and sharpen the legal-lift OEQ; then retain the hazard-lift identification theorem as the field-level kernel while anchoring the negative results to concrete published comparators.
